summary: The exact candidate corrects the reported Muse grammar arming boundary in failing-before/passing-after and adversarial state-machine tests, but its per-token rollback snapshots copy the complete reasoning history and cause quadratic retained memory, so changes are requested before acceptance.

tests.what_was_measured: Imported the prepared checkout source and reproduced masking at position 6 versus answer-body position 11; the grammar accepted the five header tokens plus body.
Masking began at answer-body position 11 and only body tokens were accepted by the inner grammar.
Candidate regression and related parser/constrained behavior: 153 passed, 64 subtests passed.

Independent boundary, repeated-reasoning, rollback/replay, copy-adjacent state, cap, no-reasoning, and detector opt-in contracts passed; also measured 4,002,000 copied history slots and 32,144,000 bytes of answer-snapshot lists for a 2,000+2,000 token stream.
Candidate diff has no whitespace errors.

gpu_execution.evidence: One AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950 was visible through Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2, but the reviewed defect is CPU-side grammar state and no GPU kernel or model inference was run.

remaining_counterexamples: A 2,000-token reasoning prefix plus 2,000 answer tokens retains 4,002,000 copied reasoning-history slots (32,144,000 bytes in copied list storage alone), demonstrating quadratic per-request memory growth in the candidate rollback snapshots.
remaining_limitations: Muse Glimmer 30B NVFP4 weights were unavailable, so production placeholder frequency, semantic quality, and full HTTP serving were not reproduced.
GPT-OSS channel framing was not verified.
No GPU execution was relevant to or used for this Python state-machine review.
No native files changed; a native rebuild was not applicable.
